text: Languages that don't exist. Procedurally generated grammars — random morphemes, random phoneme inventories, conditioned rules. Can frontier models learn them? This is the eval.

Every linguistics eval hands the model a scaffold: a morpheme bank, a worked example, a fixed template. We asked what happens when the language itself is invented — vowel harmony, noun-class agreement, conditioned suppletion — so memorization is impossible by construction. Seedable. Unlimited. Contamination-proof.

The task: twenty-four puzzles per dataset, each a miniature language with bilingual evidence pairs and queries requiring novel morphological composition. Grading is deterministic — exact morpheme match, character F-one, morpheme F-one. No language-model judge. Every answer verifiable.

Here's the boundary. With the scaffold — morpheme bank included — frontier models score near-perfect, even when we cipher the orthography or shrink the evidence. The scaffold is the hidden variable in linguistics evals. It was carrying the score.

Remove the frame and the pack splits. On generated languages: Gemini point nine seven, GPT point nine zero, Claude Opus point seven three, Qwen three-next point two eight. Errors concentrate exactly on conditioned structure — the right frame, the wrong variant. Wrong suppletive stem. Wrong harmony allomorph. Wrong agreement slot.

We made it harder. Consonant-class harmony — an arbitrary set of initial consonants, no phonetic shortcut. Then polypersonal agreement: one verb answers to two nouns at once, a prefix keyed to the subject's last sound, a suffix to the object's first, tense fused inside both. Frontier models drop further.

And on real olympiad problems — Linguini, actual IOL tasks — every model sits between point four three and point six three exact match. The limitation isn't morphology. It's discovering the structure of the problem itself.

Every number is reproducible. Stored raw generations — re-grade for zero dollars. Gold answers forty-two of forty-two, corrupted answers zero false passes. Fresh seeds generate fresh languages judges can test themselves. The eval is the artifact.
